details: Bitcoin briefly reclaimed the $80,000 mark on November 4th, accelerating its recovery after the U.S. elections and a weaker U.S. dollar, despite earlier outflows from spot Bitcoin ETFs. This rally was part of a broader recovery in crypto markets alongside Wall Street. However, on November 5th, Bitcoin experienced a sharp decline, falling from $78,767 to $75,986 within an hour. This drop was triggered by a sell-off in Nasdaq chip stocks and led to over $560 million in leveraged long position liquidations, amplifying the downward pressure.
title: Bitcoin Rebounds Above $80K, Then Drops Below $76K Amid Liquidations

details: Ethereum saw a significant jump of 6.6% on November 4th, reaching $2,422.27 and retesting its recent range high, partly fueled by a post-U.S. election rally. This recovery compressed two weeks of losses into a single session. However, on November 5th, ETH fell back toward $2,240 after its recovery toward $2,450 failed, leaving its November outlook dependent on defending support levels. Despite the price dip, U.S. Ethereum spot ETFs recorded a net inflow of $53 million on November 4th, with BlackRock's ETHA leading with $32.8 million and Fidelity's FETH with $19.2 million.
title: Ethereum Jumps Over 6% to $2,422, Then Retests Support

details: US spot Bitcoin ETFs registered a net inflow of $75 million on November 4th, marking the first positive session after three consecutive days of withdrawals. Fidelity's FBTC led the inflows with $237 million, successfully offsetting a $201 million net outflow from BlackRock's IBIT. Other funds like ARKB, BITB, and BTCO also attracted money. This reversal in trend followed significant outflows in late October and early November.
title: US Spot Bitcoin ETFs Record $75 Million Net Inflow on Nov 4

details: On November 5th, Trump Media reportedly transferred 4,259 Bitcoin, valued at approximately $343.7 million, to Crypto.com. While the move sparked sell-off fears, the coins appear to be linked to collateral for the company's 2028 convertible notes, and no sale has been confirmed. Trump Media has previously described similar transfers as custody or trading management. The company reported holding about 14,139 BTC as of July 31st.
title: Trump Media Transfers 4,259 Bitcoin to Crypto.com Exchange

details: Zcash's upcoming NU7 upgrade, designed for faster transactions, could render approximately $15 million to $16 million worth of ZEC inaccessible to owners. This is because 12,224 ZEC remain in the cryptocurrency's oldest privacy pool, "Sprout," which will stop accepting withdrawals once the upgrade is activated. This poses a significant risk for holders who have not migrated their funds.
title: Zcash Upgrade Threatens to Lock $16M in Old Privacy Pool

details: Former Bitcoin mining giant Bitfarms, now rebranded as Keel Infrastructure, has liquidated its entire Bitcoin treasury, selling 2,520 BTC for $192 million in Q3 2026. This strategic move accelerates its transition away from Bitcoin mining to focus on artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure. The company plans to sell all newly mined Bitcoin daily to avoid price volatility exposure.
title: Keel Infrastructure (Formerly Bitfarms) Sells All Bitcoin for AI Transition

details: BitPay launched a new in-app feature on November 5th, enabling eligible users to purchase cryptocurrency with a single tap using familiar payment methods like Apple Pay, Google Pay, debit/credit cards, and SEPA transfers. Powered by MoonPay, this functionality is available on iOS and Android in over 100 countries, including the U.S. and supported EU nations, delivering crypto directly to the user's self-custody wallet.
title: BitPay Wallet Adds One-Tap Crypto Buying with Apple Pay, Google Pay
